storyboard.claim: The Paul D versus Sethe clash is the book's central conflict.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D and Sethe face off, one of them thinking hard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the tin-box idea of a man who shut down to survive.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the conflict as a clash between two people, not an abstract idea.

storyboard.claim: Paul D closed his ledger of feeling to survive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D with a closed ledger book, face empty.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets Paul D against Sethe, who does the opposite.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledger metaphor is shown as a literal account book the viewer can read.

storyboard.claim: Sethe fiercely claimed her children as her own property.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, angry, pointing at what is hers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The opposite of Paul D shutting his ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Claiming is shown as a fierce gesture, not a warm one.

storyboard.claim: Paul D confronts Sethe with a newspaper clipping of her face.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D pointing at a paper clipping in the keeping room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the ledger idea to the scene of the confrontation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clipping is a real paper object, so the viewer sees the evidence.

storyboard.claim: Sethe cannot stay still while she is confronted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe walking in a circle across the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the confrontation from the clipping.
storyboard.addedInformation: The restless walk shows the pressure she is under.

storyboard.claim: Sethe is trying to explain what cannot be explained.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad, thinking hard, searching for words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Her pacing turns into an attempt to explain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the effort of the explanation, not only its content.

storyboard.claim: Sethe saw the schoolteacher's hat outside her house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, afraid, remembering the hat at the door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sethe begins to explain what she did before.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the threat that made her act: the schoolteacher's arrival.

storyboard.claim: Sethe moved her precious parts through a veil to safety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door as the passage Sethe moved through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues her account of the moment she saw the hat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door icon shows the passage to the other side, not a real escape route.

storyboard.claim: Sethe's love works as a property claim.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, worried, thinking about what she owns.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the explanation of the veil.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames love in the book's own ledger language.

storyboard.claim: In Sethe's accounting her children were the only clean part of her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad, reflecting on what stayed clean.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the property claim in her own terms.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clean versus dirty is the emotional logic of the claim.

storyboard.claim: The schoolteacher's ledger listed Sethe's traits as if she were an animal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The schoolteacher with a notebook of traits, smirking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the world that did that to her.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notebook is the ledger that reduced her to property.

storyboard.claim: In that world Sethe had zero value, but her children were her best thing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad, slumped under the weight of the valuation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the schoolteacher's ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: The zero is named in the callout, not staged as violence.

storyboard.claim: Sethe claims her children to void the schoolteacher's claim over them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, angry, pointing away at the schoolteacher.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sethe's claim is the answer to the schoolteacher's ledger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the claim as a contest between two people.

storyboard.claim: Sethe tells the room that no one can own her children.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, angry, speaking firmly from the shed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Her defiant line leads into the clash with Paul D.
storyboard.addedInformation: The quoted line is set as the callout so the defiance is readable.

storyboard.claim: Paul D is terrified and tells Sethe her love is too thick.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D, afraid, facing Sethe who does not apologize.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Her defiance now meets his fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: Paul D's accusation is the callout, so the viewer hears what he fears.

storyboard.claim: Sethe stands her ground: love is either total or it is not love.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, angry, standing firm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Her answer to Paul D's accusation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout carries the quoted line in full.

storyboard.claim: Thin love is not love at all, and Sethe refuses fractional love.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, angry, pointing down at her own rule.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues her refusal of partial love.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the rejection of fractions into the callout.

storyboard.claim: There is no partial love and no loving just enough to survive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, worried, thinking about what survival would cost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates her refusal in plain terms.
storyboard.addedInformation: The short callout is the narrator's own phrase.

storyboard.claim: Sethe rejects the fractional math of slavery and the division of families.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains as the system she rejects, Sethe pointing at it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens from her personal refusal to the system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read as bondage, the system itself, not as links.

storyboard.claim: The narrator asks whether they are letting Sethe off the hook, and sides with Paul D.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D, worried, thinking about the wreckage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from Sethe's position to the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the critical question into the callout.

storyboard.claim: For a formerly enslaved woman, loving too thick is a lethal vulnerability.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, afraid, exposed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Paul D's view is sound.
storyboard.addedInformation: The vulnerability is the danger the narrator names.

storyboard.claim: Paul D thinks the safest thing is to love just a little.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D, sad, thinking about his survival math.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives Paul D's position from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout is the narrator's phrase for his strategy.

storyboard.claim: Paul D's survival math is to keep a little love in reserve.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D holding notes that carry his calculation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the math from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes object shows the calculation as a written account.

storyboard.claim: Sethe's thick love destroyed her family and drove her sons away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad, slumped with the cost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the consequences of her love.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cost is named in the callout, not in an abstract family icon.

storyboard.claim: Her thick love brought a destructive haunting upon her house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A house icon, Sethe afraid in the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequences of the thick love now reach the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The house icon is the literal home the haunting enters.

storyboard.claim: The host asks the audience to view Sethe through maternal determinism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D, worried, thinking about the lens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the case for her defense.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the critical lens in the callout.

callout.text: THE WORLD VALUED HER FAMILY AT ZERO

storyboard.claim: Sethe had to love thick because the world valued her family at zero.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad, in the room.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE WORLD VALUED HER FAMILY AT ZERO
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Unpacks the lens from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The zero valuation is the claim the callout states.

storyboard.claim: The schoolteacher's ledger treats a child as future labor and property.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The schoolteacher with a ledger, smirking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the ledger that values the family at zero.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledger is a notes object, so the record is visible.

storyboard.claim: Sethe's thick love was the only counterweight to the schoolteacher's math.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance as Sethe's love against the ledger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why loving just a little would be surrender.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance shows weighing two sides, not a verdict.

storyboard.claim: Sethe had to love with absolute, terrifying density to fight the system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, afraid, holding her ground.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the counterweight argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: The density is stated as the callout, the narrator's own phrase.

storyboard.claim: Slavery counted people as property, while a mother counted her children as love.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad, thinking about the two ledgers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up the collision of the two ledgers.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two ledgers are named as opposites in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Sethe's arithmetic of isolating herself with her best things starves the household.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door as exclusion, Sethe sad beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the cost of the friction between the ledgers.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door shows exclusion from the outside world.

storyboard.claim: Thick love leads to a closed household that starves.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from thick love to a closed ecosystem to starvation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the isolation from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flow makes the cause and effect explicit.

storyboard.claim: Denver walks out the door, the turning point of the novel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver walking through a door toward the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the closed household that starves.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door marks the outside world that Denver enters.

storyboard.claim: Denver has not left the yard of 124 since she was a girl.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver afraid, with the Bluestone road behind her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why her walk out is a turning point.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road is the literal Bluestone Road she never left.

storyboard.claim: Sethe and Beloved are locked in a fatal loop of starvation and obsession.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe worried beside Beloved, both thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The unsustainable math inside the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fatal loop is stated as the callout.

storyboard.claim: Beloved demands more while Sethe wastes away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Beloved, angry, demanding, with Sethe behind her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the loop from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The demand is named in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Sethe spends her life savings until nothing is left.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, sad, with an empty account of her savings.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the cost of the loop in the household's money.
storyboard.addedInformation: The empty account is the callout, not a coin object.

storyboard.claim: Denver realises she must leave, and steps off the edge of the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Denver afraid, walking off the porch into the winter street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why she leaves the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The edge is the moment she leaves the yard.

storyboard.claim: Denver walks to the home of her former teacher, Lady Jones.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A home icon, Denver worried at the door of a house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leads to Denver reaching the outside world.
storyboard.addedInformation: The home icon is the literal house of the former teacher.
